newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs at 6-week lows, pork bellies down sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs at 6-week lows, pork bellies down sharply.

text.p: CME hog futures fell to six-week lows on fund liquidation and sell stops while pork belly futures dropped sharply on technical sell stops. A weak tone to cash markets pushed futures down into the technical selling, traders said.
Hog futures closed 1.000 to 0.025 lower with April off 0.750 at 73.300 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.950 to 0.750 lower with March off most at 75.200 cents.
Fund liquidation and sell stops took hog futures down to lowest levels since December 30, the first trading day after the December pig crop report, they said.
"We're filling in the gap left on the charts after the (Hog and Pigs) report," one trader said.

Lower cash hog markets and expectations of lower live prices again Tuesday provided early fundamental pressure. The cash pork product market remains under pressure despite a cutback in the rate of slaughter and packers will continue to lower bids for hogs and cut kills to improve cutout margins, traders said.
Rand Financials, Cargill Investor Services, R.J. O'Brien, ADM Investor Services and Fimat Futures USA sold April, pit sources said.

In hog options, commission houses sold deep in the money February 78 puts early and sold 74 and 75 puts late. Locals bought 70 to 74 April puts. LIT division of First Options bought April 76 calls, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures plummeted in a sharp reversal of Friday's gains as concern over cash markets pushed prices down into technical sell stops. The continued weak tone to cash bellies despite reduced kills and apparent increased numbers going into frozen storage prompted selling, traders said.
Some long liquidation was also cited in February ahead of first deliveries Tuesday.

Expectations are that up to 50 deliveries may be posted against February before it expires later in the month. Certified deliverable stocks have been rising and total storage stocks could equal or exceed last year's level if product keeps moving into storage, they added.
Cargill and LFG notably sold March late. Rand Financials sold February early while ADM Investor Services bought, pit sources said.
